label: lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant
title: Two antiderivatives differ by a constant
statement: If $F$ and $G$ are antiderivatives of $f$ on $(a,b)$, both continuous on $[a,b]$, then $(F-G)(x) = (F-G)(a)$ for all $x \in [a,b]$.
proof: By Lemma~\ref{lem:antideriv_diff_zero_deriv}, $F-G$ has zero derivative on $(a,b)$. Since $F-G$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, Lemma~\ref{lem:zero_deriv_constant} gives the result.
